--- title: "JupyterLab" jupyter: php --- ## Notebooks {#starting-a-notebook} Start JupyterLab from the Python environment that has it: ```bash ~/.venvs/juphyter/bin/jupyter lab ``` The launcher lists each kernel juphyter registered under its display name, such as "PHP 8.5" for the default `php` kernel and "PHP (PHPstats)" for the kernel from [Installation](install.qmd#the-phpstats-packages). A notebook that is already open changes kernel through **Kernel > Change Kernel**. JupyterLab finds kernels in the per-user Jupyter data directory and in `JUPYTER_DATA_DIR` when it is set. `jupyter kernelspec list` shows the kernels a JupyterLab started from the same environment will find. ## Cells {#running-cells} A cell's result appears under it as `Out[n]`. State carries from one cell to the next. The stop button interrupts a running cell when PHP has the `pcntl` extension, and **Kernel > Restart Kernel** starts a new PHP session with nothing defined. Tab completion covers three cases: - Variables in the session, after a `$`. - Declared functions and classes, for a bare prefix. - Public methods, properties, and constants, after `->` or `::`. An unfinished block or string keeps the cell open for another line instead of running it. ## Project classes Jupyter starts the kernel in the notebook's directory. The kernel looks upward from there for `vendor/autoload.php`, so a notebook saved inside a Composer project can use that project's classes and packages. A notebook kept outside the project it works on names the autoloader in a `juphyter.json` beside it: ```json { "autoload": "../app/vendor/autoload.php" } ``` [Autoloading](install.qmd#which-classes-a-notebook-sees) lists every way to set it. ## Tables and plots A phibble data frame appears as an HTML table with its dimensions and column types. The table follows JupyterLab's light and dark themes. The table below is [weather](https://github.com/phpstats/datasets#weather): hourly observations at New York's three airports in 2013, from R's `nycflights13` package. ::: {#a96b9027 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.php .cell-code} DataFrame::fromCsv( 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/' .'phpstats/datasets/main/csv/weather.csv' ); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: A phiz plot appears as a chart. JupyterLab draws it from its Vega-Lite specification and needs no extension. juphyter publishes a plot's specification under `application/vnd.vegalite.v5+json`, the Vega-Lite type that JupyterLab's built-in renderer reads. A plot also carries a static SVG, which JupyterLab does not use, for Quarto's PDF and Word output. ## Conversion {#converting-a-notebook} `quarto convert` turns a `.ipynb` into a `.qmd` and back, and `jupyter nbconvert` exports a notebook to HTML or PDF. Both work on a PHP notebook, because they read the notebook file format and not the language.
